Printed shipping cartons

Specifying a color printed corrugated shipping carton

FORME Packaging editorialUpdated October 21, 20263 min read

A printed shipping case needs to communicate the brand and carry the complete shipment. Start with the four-flap construction, then define the board, protection and print scope.

In this guideRecognize the four-flap shipping caseSpecify the filled shipmentChoose the printing route with the supplierWhat to include in the inquiryDiscuss your packaging →

Recognize the four-flap shipping case

A standard 0201-style regular slotted case has flaps at the top and bottom. The major outer flaps meet along the center when closed; the packed case needs a suitable sealing method. This differs from a die-cut mailer with a single rear-hinged lid and folded locking sidewalls.

A style code describes construction, rather than the complete performance specification. Record internal dimensions, board construction, flute, liner and strength requirements separately. Ask for the exact structural drawing when a variant is proposed.

Specify the filled shipment

Provide the weight, number and arrangement of the packed products. Explain whether the case will hold individual retail cartons, bottles, ceramic pieces or mixed goods. Include the delivery route and any stacking or storage requirements known to your team.

Dividers and end supports should match the actual products. For bottles, check separation at the widest points and support near the neck where appropriate. For homeware, prevent products from contacting one another during handling. Validate the complete filled pack using an agreed test plan.

Choose the printing route with the supplier

Direct printing on a suitable liner and laminating a printed sheet onto corrugated board offer different production routes. Discuss the artwork, coverage, order quantity and desired surface. A full-color design still needs clear fold lines, adhesive areas and sealing zones.

Keep handling symbols, shipping labels and barcodes in usable positions. Do not place an essential label across the center closure without checking the packing process. Review a decorated sample after it has been folded and sealed.

What to include in the inquiry

  • Internal dimensions and fully packed weight.
  • Case construction, board and strength proposal.
  • Partitions, protective fitments and sealing method.
  • Printed panels, artwork and coating requirements.
  • Quantity, destination and packed shipment testing.
